'''Bisque''' or '''bisk'''<ref>[https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bisk Merriam-Webster entry for ''bisk'']</ref><ref>[https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bisk Collins English Dictionary entry for ''bisk'']</ref> ({{IPA|fr|bisk|-|LL-Q150 (fra)-LoquaxFR-bisque.wav}}; {{langx|oc|Bisca}}) is a smooth, creamy, highly seasoned [[soup]] of [[France|French]] origin, classically based on a strained broth ([[coulis]]) of [[crustacean]]s.<ref>The ''Académie Française Dictionary'' defines a bisque as: "BISQUE n. Potage fait d'un coulis de crustacés. Une bisque de homard, d'écrevisses." ("Soup made from a crustacean coulis, e.g. lobster or crayfish bisque.")</ref> It can be made from [[Lobster meat|lobster]], [[langoustine]], [[Crab meat|crab]], [[Shrimp and prawn as food|shrimp]], or [[crayfish as food|crayfish]]. The French bisque is one of the most popular seafood soups around the world.

Although originally applied to seafood soups, the use of the word has expanded to mean any thick soup made with cream, such as bisque of tomato or bisque of mushroom. It is differentiated from a [[chowder]], also a seafood soup, by its consistency, a chowder being less smooth and more chunky.
